holidays.name: National Wear Your Pajamas to Work Day
holidays.description: Employees swap stiff office attire for flannel, fuzzy slippers, and novelty sleepwear. It's a day to prove that productivity and comfort can coexist, even if your bunny slippers are judging your spreadsheets.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, informal observance that spread through workplaces and social media as part of the broader comfort-at-work movement. There is no single documented founder, and it is celebrated in various forms by different companies.
holidays.funFact: Pajamas come from the Hindi/Urdu word 'pae jama,' meaning 'leg garment.' British colonists in India adopted the loose trousers and brought them home as sleepwear in the 1800s.

holidays.name: National Eggs Benedict Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the glorious brunch classic: a toasted English muffin topped with Canadian bacon, a poached egg, and a blanket of buttery hollandaise sauce.
holidays.origin: Food-day observances like this one are generally unofficial and come from culinary calendars. The dish's origin is disputed, with stories tracing it to Delmonico's restaurant or to the Waldorf Hotel in New York City in the late 1800s.
holidays.funFact: One origin story claims a hungover Wall Street broker named Lemuel Benedict ordered the dish at the Waldorf Hotel in 1894 as a cure, and the maître d' put it on the menu.

holidays.name: Save the Elephant Day
holidays.description: An awareness day devoted to protecting elephants from poaching, habitat loss, and captivity. Participants learn about conservation and support sanctuaries around the world.
holidays.origin: Founded as a conservation awareness campaign, it is observed on April 16 to spotlight the plight of elephants, which are threatened across Africa and Asia.
holidays.funFact: Elephants are one of the few animals that appear to hold funeral-like rituals, gathering around the remains of dead herd members and touching their bones with their trunks.

holidays.name: Wilbur Wright Birthday
holidays.description: A nod to the birthday of Wilbur Wright, the aviation pioneer who, together with his brother Orville, made the first controlled, powered airplane flight. People mark it with paper airplane contests and flight-themed fun.
holidays.origin: Wilbur Wright was born on April 16, 1867, near Millville, Indiana. The observance grew from aviation enthusiasts and history fans celebrating his birth.
holidays.funFact: The Wright brothers ran a bicycle shop in Dayton, Ohio, and used a homemade wind tunnel to test wing designs before their famous flight at Kitty Hawk in 1903.

holidays.name: National Librarian Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the keepers of books, quiet corners, and mysteriously reliable search skills. Librarians get appreciated for guiding people to information and stories.
holidays.origin: This is an informal appreciation day observed on April 16 in the United States. It complements the larger National Library Week celebrated in April.
holidays.funFact: The Dewey Decimal System, which many librarians still use, was created in 1876 by Melvil Dewey when he was just 25 years old.
